query: The extracellular signals were unity-gain buffered, filtered (600 Hz–6 kHz), amplified (gain = 5000), and continuously sampled at 25 kHz.

query: One channel of each electrode was duplicated for detecting LFPs and was filtered (0.1 Hz–6 kHz) and amplified (gain = 500).

query: The LFP recordings were further band-pass filtered (150–250 Hz) using the Hilbert transform.

query: Local peaks in the power of this filtered signal of magnitude >mean + 3SD were identified and extracted as periods. The boundaries for each period were defined as the point at which the amplitude crossed the mean. Periods during which running speed was <2 cm/s were identified as SWR events.

query: After spike sorting as previously described (Takahashi et al., 2003; Takahashi and Sakurai, 2009; Takahashi, 2013), putative principal cells were distinguished from putative fast-spiking cells based on spike width (0.4 ms) and average firing rate (5 Hz).

query: Spikes during delay periods in the DA subtask, when hippocampal activity was not place-specific (Pastalkova et al., 2008), were excluded.

query: Spatial bins had a resolution of approximately 2 cm.

query: Time windows for task performance and replays were set at 250 ms and 20 ms, respectively.

query: To minimize ambiguous detections, periods were decreased based on the following criteria. query: Secondly, for each period, the rat's location was decoded using the Bayesian decoder, for 20-ms time windows advanced in 5-ms increments.

query: Fourthly, two significance tests were conducted for every candidate, using a Monte Carlo method with two different random shuffling modes: cell identity and cell place field (5000 times each).

query: Firstly, a binary population vector, C, was constructed. This vector could exist in one of two states, high or low.
